pr_title: Child requests proactively cancel children tasks
pr_body:
To make this possible we modify the CancellableTasksTracker to track children tasks by the Request ID as well. That way, we can send an Action to cancel a child based on the parent task and the Request ID.

This is especially useful when parents' children requests timeout on the parents' side.

The motivation behind this PR lies behind fixing test failure #90353. In discussing the simple solution of PR https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/92520, we decided with @DaveCTurner that the best approach to solving the test failure would be to solve #66992. Unfortunately that issue may require substantial effort. But for the moment, we thought it would be easier to cancel children requests on timeout, since we already have infrastructure for tracking children tasks (through the `CancellableTasksTracker`).

Fixes #90353
Relates #66992

issue_context.title: Cancel task (and descendants) if its originating transport request times out
issue_context.body:
If a sender sets a timeout on a transport request and does not receive a response in time then today we make no attempt to inform the receiver that we no longer care about its response. This is particularly bad for stats requests that may be timing out on one broken node, but still continue to pile up there since that node has no way to know that these requests are now irrelevant and should not be processed.

A couple of possible solutions spring to mind:

- When the sender times out it could sends a task cancellation request to the receiver.

- The sender could indicate the timeout to the receiver, which could then implement its own local timeout-and-cancel behaviour.

Relates https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/60188, https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/52616, https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/51992.
comments: Thanks @DaveCTurner, Is it a prioritised item already, if not I'd be interested to work on this

We're still contemplating how/whether to proceed on this. We may take no action since this only really applies to internally-generated requests which are mostly fairly well-behaved already. @Bukhtawar perhaps you'd be interested in resolving https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/55550 instead? Supporting cancellation on stats APIs would address the concerns you raised in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/52616 for instance.
Sure @DaveCTurner I'll take up support for cancellation on stats API. I'll get back on this

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/92588 is merged which will allow parents to send a cancel action to remote children upon a parent's failure (such as a time-out in the most usual case).

I think this ticket is a bit larger than that, since it is written in a way that is not constrained only to tasks with a parent. But maybe the PR about children tasks covers a large portion of this ticket.

review_comments: I would prefer to use the node instead of the connection here, that would avoid issues if the connection is dropped for some reason.
This is a tricky assertion, something might get enqueued just after the assertion. But I think `ensureBansAndCancellationsConsistency` covers most of what we want to assert here.

This is necessary because it seems otherwise the test infrastructure may get stuck. If I remember correctly, it's probably because the test at the end then thinks that sometimes things are still running (servers received cancellation but did not make it to process it). That is why I wait for the thread pools to be empty. I do not think anything else can get enqueued afterwards, but if anything does I would expect it to be done by the end of the test procedure.

An alternative here instead of re-throwing with a RuntimeException would be to make the org.elasticsearch.common.util.CancellableThreads.Interruptible interface to throw also an IOException or an Exception in general instead of only an InterruptedException (that it currently allows). Feedback is welcome on this point.
I think we should just do proactive checking with `task.ensureNotCancelled()` at different stages to avoid the extra complexity, wdyt?

I am not sure we can do this. In this case, the original [test failing](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/90353) is because the single snapshot thread here is stuck inside the `writeBlob()` function in the lucene's RateLimiter with a very long sleep. So the only way out of it with an interruption, and the `cancellableThreads` here is the most straightforward way I found that we support doing this (its .cancel() sends an interrupt).

Further reading CancellableThreads class, I see it especially handles any thrown runtime exception back, so I think wrapping the IOException in a runtime exception is the expected way of doing it.

I wonder if doing a linear search using the previous approach from `Map<TaskId, T[]>` would be enough and will simplify all this code. For that we would need to store the `requestId` in the `CancellableTaskHolder` or something like that. 
I mention this since the `put` method mentions that it's expected to be called only once per task and now that we have this notion of `requestId` that you mention that it can be -1 multiple times (when is that possible? we set the requestId for all incoming requests and local requests are not tracked here)

Hmm, CancellableTasksTracker<T> is generic and is instantiated indeed with <CancellableTaskHolder> in production but also with <String> in testing. That is why I extended it here with a Map to put the request ID, because putting the requestId in T would mean to do it in a way that satisfied both production and test code. Plus I thought the Map gives some performance advantage over the linear search in both putting (since it puts in the Map, instead of replacing a whole array) and in searching.

> -1 multiple times (when is that possible? we set the requestId for all incoming requests and local requests are not tracked here)

I do not believe there is a requirement that all tasks emanate from requests, and that is why we had thought it safe (when I was originally discussing this with @DaveCTurner ) to also consider -1 just in case. Please note though that `cancelChildLocal()` calls this new method only when the request ID to be cancelled is positive.
